app.title: Safari Ad Blocker
app.subtitle: Three Safari content blockers plus a video ad skipper. Each one can be turned on or off in Safari settings.
language.label: Language
language.note: Extension names inside Safari's own settings follow the system language.
ext.Ads.name: Ad Blocking
ext.Ads.detail: EasyList plus your own rules (filters/custom.txt). Blocks banners, pop-ups and ad scripts, and hides ad placeholders.
ext.Privacy.name: Tracker Blocking
ext.Privacy.detail: EasyPrivacy. Blocks analytics and tracking scripts and beacons.
ext.Korea.name: Korean Sites Ad Blocking
ext.Korea.detail: List-KR and YousList. Rules specific to Korean sites such as Naver and Daum.
ext.VideoAdSkip.name: Video Ad Skipper
ext.VideoAdSkip.detail: Skips pre-roll and mid-roll video ads automatically and dismisses ad-blocker warnings. After enabling it, Safari asks for site access the first time you open the video site; choose ‘Always Allow’.
state.off: Off — turn it on in Safari
help.title: How to use
help.step1: Turn on the four items in Safari › Settings › Extensions. The button below opens that screen.
help.profiles: If you use Safari profiles (a profile icon at the left of the tab bar), each profile must be turned on separately: Safari › Settings › Profiles › the profile › Extensions tab. The ‘On’ shown here refers to the default profile.
help.step2: To turn blocking off for one site only, open that site and choose Safari menu › ‘Settings for <site>…’ › uncheck ‘Enable content blockers’.
help.step3: The ‘Check It Works’ button opens a test site so you can confirm blocking is active. Pages that were already open must be reloaded after enabling.
help.step4: To update the block lists, run ./update-rules.sh in the project folder and then ./install.sh.
help.video: Video ads cannot be blocked by content blockers, so ‘Video Ad Skipper’ ends them inside the page instead. It may stop working for a while when the site changes its structure.
help.unsigned: This build is signed ad hoc (no certificate). Turn on Safari › Settings › Advanced › ‘Show features for web developers’, then Develop › Developer Settings… › ‘Allow unsigned extensions’ for the extensions to appear. Safari resets that setting when it quits, so sign with an Apple Development certificate for regular use (see README).
msg.reloadTimeout: Safari did not respond within 20 seconds. The rules may have been reloaded anyway; reload a page in Safari to check.
msg.settingsFailed: Could not open Safari settings automatically ({error}). Enable the extensions in Safari › Settings › Extensions.
msg.testFailed: Could not open the test site: {error}
msg.testOpened: Opened the test site in Safari. A high score (80 or more) means the rules are active. Both Ad Blocking and Tracker Blocking must be on for a high score.
